title: Interventional Tensor Fabric Memory

predecessor.name: Fabric-Induced Memory bounded component study
predecessor.summary: The frozen 24-cell study did not establish general necessity of memory, retrieval, or salience gating. Directions split 3/6 and the smallest exact sign-test p-value was 0.5.
prohibited_actions: rerun the frozen predecessor to seek a favorable result
present successor development as independent reproduction

research_question: Under partial observation with oracle-defined aliasing, does an owner-safe transport-aligned tensor-valued external memory provide forecast-relevant information beyond matched finite-history, recurrent, state-space, and analytical transport predictors, and is that information localized by memory-only interventions?
scientific_objective: Identify whether external tensor memory contains uniquely useful spatiotemporal information rather than merely adding capacity, context, compute, or an optimization path.
hypothesis: On aliased states whose current observations are insufficient for predicting the future, an owner-safe, past-only tensor memory storing spatial residual fields in an age-aware constant-velocity co-moving coordinate system will improve the predeclared alias-conditioned forecast endpoint over matched learned, sham, transport-off, and analytical transport controls; erasing the relevant values will remove the benefit, and swapping them between oracle alias pairs will shift forecasts toward the donor future without materially harming non-aliased controls.
falsifiers: A matched finite-history or recurrent-state control is within the practical-equivalence margin or better on the primary endpoint.
Erasing eligible memory does not cause the predeclared degradation on aliased cases.
Value swaps do not move forecasts toward the donor future in the predeclared direction.
Random or nuisance-matched values perform equivalently to true eligible values.
Any advantage disappears after matching parameters, training updates, accessible information, and tuning budget.
The effect occurs only in the synthetic development system and fails the future public-domain replication.
intended_contribution: An intervention-based mechanism-identification protocol and reference implementation for spatially structured external memory under partial observability, not a claim that tensors, transport, or external memory are novel by themselves.

in: query-aligned tensor keys and residual values
bounded normalized-cross-correlation transport and age-aware co-moving coordinates
rank-generic fabric operators for one two and three dimensional fields
out: confirmatory claims before a protected public-data protocol is frozen

budgets.development_scope: 27 predeclared cells: nine models across three paired seeds after Checkpoint 6. Eight models are learned and one bounded-cross-correlation transport baseline is analytical; sensitivity reuses primary checkpoints without retraining.
budgets.compute: CPU or Apple MPS only; no cloud spend; no full run while free plus speculative memory is below 512 MiB or pageouts are increasing.
budgets.protected_evaluation: Not created. No protected test outcomes may be inspected until a versioned confirmatory protocol is frozen.

primary_endpoint: Alias-conditioned one-step normalized MSE, aggregated first within trajectory and then across independent paired families.
mechanism_endpoints: retrieval precision against oracle regime labels
practical_effect_rule: Development candidate requires at least 5% relative improvement over the strongest matched learned control on alias-conditioned NMSE and the correct directional response for erasure and value-swap endpoints. This is a development gate, not a confirmatory claim.

supported: The predecessor is a completed bounded negative study.
The successor question is falsifiable and separated from the predecessor.
The successor contribution is intervention-based identification, not generic external memory.
unsupported: Tensor memory is more powerful than vector memory.
The successor is novel enough for publication.
The successor generalizes to natural systems.
The successor is ready for confirmatory execution.

decisions: Preserve the predecessor exactly and create a separate successor directory.
Use tensor-valued keys and observation-residual values rather than compressed vector values.
Require explicit trajectory IDs and event times for every memory operation.
Use a global vector-broadcast memory as the spatial mechanism-off control.
Use deterministic sham retrieval as the parameter- and compute-matched information control.
Predeclare context-noise, missingness, speed-shift, top-k, and transport-radius evaluations within a 27-cell development matrix.
Treat multidimensional support as an unvalidated engineering extension; keep the scientific development protocol two-dimensional.
Run numerical work at one thread and niceness 10 with admission rechecks before every model/seed cell.
Use exact search at development scale; approximate search is out of scope.
Do not select the public confirmatory dataset during development.
Use bounded normalized spatial cross-correlation, not Fourier phase correlation, and name the operator exactly.
Require transport-off, sham-transport, analytical periodic-transport, finite-history, recurrent, and stable diagonal-SSM controls.
known_failures: The predecessor memory and retrieval components showed no stable general benefit.
The predecessor vector memory broadcast one update across all spatial locations.
Earlier spatial-recall FIM lost to zero and history controls under the tested budget.
The current outer checkout has unresolved tracked-deletion and untracked-relocation lineage.
The first admitted successor test run used Python 3.14 and failed before collection because pytest was absent; its failure receipt is retained.

The first Python 3.11 test run found a 3D test fixture missing its channel axis: 36 tests passed and one fixture failed. The fixture was corrected without changing the model, and the next run passed 37/37.
The smoke experiment imported Torch and paused before its first cell when post-import free-plus-speculative memory was 473333760 bytes; zero runs and zero model failures were retained.
